'''Riccardo Levi-Setti''' (July 11, 1927 – November 8, 2018<ref name=uc>{{cite news|url=https://news.uchicago.edu/story/riccardo-levi-setti-physicist-and-trilobite-collector-1927-2018|title=Riccardo Levi-Setti, physicist and trilobite collector, 1927–2018|website=UChicago News|publisher=University of Chicago Office of Communications|accessdate=April 23, 2019}}</ref>) was an Italian [[emeritus]] professor of [[physics]] and [[paleontology]] at the [[University of Chicago]]<ref>{{cite news|website=[[Phys.org]]|url=http://phys.org/news138540908.html|title=Exploding chromosomes fuel research about evolution of genetic storage|date=August 21, 2008|accessdate=April 23, 2019}}</ref> and a [[The Holocaust|Holocaust]] survivor.<ref>{{cite news|newspaper=[[The Washington Post]]|date=November 21, 2018|url=https://www.pressherald.com/2018/11/21/holocaust-survivor-who-uncovered-trilobites-and-subatomic-particles-dies/|title=Holocaust survivor who uncovered trilobites and subatomic particles dies|publisher=Press Herald|author=Harrison Smith|accessdate=April 23, 2019}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Riccardo was born in Milan in 1927 to Paolo and Gilda Levi, a decorated lieutenant colonel in the Italian army of [[World War I]] and a Venetian [[aristocrat]].<ref name=uc/> His family fled to [[Pavia]] after [[Benito Mussolini]] ordered a crackdown on [[Jews]] in his hometown. As a result of migration, he obtained his doctorate in [[physics]] from the [[University of Pavia]] in 1952 and then was awarded a [[Fulbright Program|Fulbright Scholarship]] to go to the [[United States]].<ref name=ct>{{cite news|author=Graydon Megan|url=http://www.chicagotribune.com/news/obituaries/ct-met-levi-setti-obituary-20181121-story.html|title=Riccardo Levi-Setti, U. of C. physicist whose interests included ancient sea creatures, dies|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|date=November 23, 2018|access-date=April 23, 2019}}</ref>

==Career==
Riccardo joined [[University of Chicago]] in 1956, upon invitation from [[Enrico Fermi]].<ref name=ct/> There he started his career as an assistant professor of [[particle physics]] and by 1963 was promoted to tenure professor. He contributed to the discovery of neutral [[kaon]] decay, for which [[James Cronin]] was awarded with the [[Nobel Prize in Physics|Nobel Prize]] a year later. Riccardo became full professor in 1965, and in 1970s had shifted his research toward [[ion]] [[microscopy]]. From 1992 to 2000 Riccardo had served as director of the [[Enrico Fermi Institute]], a department of the [[University of Chicago Medical Center]] where he was a pioneer in [[biology]] and [[biomedicine]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://hpherald.com/2018/11/28/riccardo-levi-setti-91/|title=Riccardo Levi-Setti, 91|work=Hyde Park Herald|date=November 28, 2018|accessdate=April 23, 2019|archive-date=April 23, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190423153511/https://hpherald.com/2018/11/28/riccardo-levi-setti-91/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Levi-Setti spent some time at [[CERN]]<ref name="cern">{{cite journal|url=https://cds.cern.ch/record/2035960/files/CERN-TC-PHYSICS-65-11.pdf|title=A search for heavy hyperon resonances produced by 5.7 GeV/c antiprotons in hydrogen|date=17 May 1965|journal=Physics Letters|volume=17|issue=2|pages=166|accessdate=2019-07-23|bibcode=1965PhL....17..166B|last1=Böck|first1=R. K.|last2=Cooper|first2=W. A.|last3=French|first3=B. R.|last4=Kinson|first4=J. B.|last5=Levi-Setti|first5=R.|last6=Revel|first6=D.|last7=Tallini|first7=B.|last8=Zylberajch|first8=S.|doi=10.1016/0031-9163(65)90285-4}}</ref><ref name="inspire">{{cite web|url=http://inspirehep.net/author/profile/R.Levi.Setti.2|title=Levi-Setti, R. - Author profile|publisher=[[INSPIRE-HEP]]|accessdate=2019-07-23}}</ref> in 1963 as a [[Guggenheim Fellowship|John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Fellow]].<ref name="gugg">{{cite web|url=https://www.gf.org/fellows/all-fellows/riccardo-levi-setti/|title=Riccardo Levi-Setti|website=John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation|accessdate=2019-07-23}}</ref>

In 2011 he, along with Roger Hildebrand, participated in the ceremony of the opening of the Enrico Fermi time capsule.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://neutrontrail.com/2011/06/enrico-fermi-time-capsule-opening/|title=Enrico Fermi Time Capsule Opening|date=June 2, 2011|accessdate=April 23, 2019}}</ref>

In 1975 he wrote a book called ''Trilobites'', which was reissued in 1993.<ref>{{cite magazine|volume=95|issue=4|date=April 2003|magazine=University of Chicago Magazine|url=https://magazine.uchicago.edu/0304/features/index-levi.html|title=Riccardo Levi-Setti — Trilobites|publisher=University of Chicago Magazine}}</ref> In 2014 his third book, called ''The Trilobite Book: A Visual Journey'', was published.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.timeshighereducation.co.uk/books/the-trilobite-book-a-visual-journey-by-riccardo-levi-setti/2015839.article|title=The Trilobite Book: A Visual Journey, by Riccardo Levi-Setti|work=[[Times Higher Education]]|date=September 25, 2014|accessdate=April 23, 2019}}</ref>

==Death and legacy==
Riccardo had died from natural causes on November 8, 2018, after a brief stay at Montgomery Place, Chicago.<ref name=ct/> After his death, his findings were donated to various museums, including the [[Field Museum of Natural History|Field Museum]] and the [[American Museum of Natural History]] as well as Manuels River Hibernia Interpretation Center in [[Newfoundland]], Canada.<ref name=uc/>

His name also present at the exhibit at [[Manuels River]], Newfoundland, Canada. In 2000, an asteroid orbiting between [[Jupiter]] and [[Mars]] was given his name as 45700 Levi-Setti.<ref name=uc/>

==Personal life==
Riccardo was married to Nika Semkoff Levi-Setti, a former teacher at the [[University of Chicago Laboratory Schools]] and former public relations manager of the [[Field Museum of Natural History]]. Together with first wife, Katharine Gould Straight, he had two sons, Emile and Matteo, who were born in 1965 and 1968 respectively. He also had two grandchildren, Allegra and Colette.<ref name=uc/>

==Awards==
*Guggenheim Fellow (1963)<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gf.org/fellows/all-fellows/riccardo-levi-setti/|title=Riccardo Levi-Setti|publisher=[[John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation]]|accessdate=April 23, 2019}}</ref>
*Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]]
*[[ASME Leonardo Da Vinci Award|Leonardo da Vinci Award]]
*Steinberg Award
